text:
anna_support: customer reports embeddings throughput drop, tokens/sec steady but vectors/sec down ~60% since 03:00 UTC. they say no schema changes on their side.

maria_oncall: thanks — any errors in the logs or 429 spikes?

anna_support: no 429s, auth ok. latency per-request up a bit. metrics: token_rate ~1.1M/s, vector_rate 420k/s (expected ~1.0M/s). GPU util at 70% but queue depth high.

kai_infra: share the dashboard link? queue depth = queued_requests per pod?

anna_support: https://grafana.internal/rd/embeds?panel=vec-rate (redacted) - summary: pod_count stable, avg_batch_size dropped from 12 -> 4 after midnight, queue_depth per node ~480, concurrency window widened.

josh_research: that smells like batching window change or client-side small batches. but tokens/sec steady suggests requests still coming in, just smaller per-request work converting to more scheduling overhead.

maria_oncall: can you paste a representative request/responses headers (strip PII)? maybe dimension mismatch forcing fallback?

anna_support: customer payload snippet: `{"model":"rwd-embed-2048","input":"...","expected_dim":1536}` they said they recently toggled a new SDK version.

kai_infra: if client expects 1536 but we serve 1024 variant as fallback, we may be doing runtime upscaling or conversion that kills throughput. check route mapping.

deploy-bot: rollback completed for routing rule rollout id rl-2026-03-17-01 (succeeded).

josh_research: log grep from router shows a lot of `model_variant_mismatch` events around 03:02:

```
2026-03-17T03:02:14Z router[info] request_id=abc123 model_requested=rwd-embed-1536 routed_to=rwd-embed-1024 variant_mismatch=true
2026-03-17T03:02:14Z runtime[warn] request_id=abc123 convert_dim: src=1536 dst=1024 performed_quant_downcast=true
2026-03-17T03:02:14Z kvcache[debug] waiters=62 queue_depth=492
```

maria_oncall: that conversion log indicates we served a smaller quantized variant. conversion step could be expensive if done per-request. are we doing on-the-fly fallback instead of pre-transcoding?

kai_infra: checking autoscaling and variant inventory: looks like after the rollout, 1024 variant was preferred in low-latency region. autoscaler pinned GPU types that have only quant-1024 kernels. we should have a fallback that redirects to a compatible 1536-backed pool but it used converter path.

anna_support: customer says they didn't change batch size. they upgraded SDK 1.8.1 -> 1.9.0 which switched to `prefer_low_mem=true` by default. could explain client requesting lower-memory variants but still expecting 1536 dims.

josh_research: repro steps I used locally:
1) curl embed endpoint with header `X-Model: rwd-embed-1536` and `Prefer-Low-Mem: true`
2) observe route header `X-Routed-Model: rwd-embed-1024` and runtime conversion.

```
curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -H "X-Model: rwd-embed-1536" -H "Prefer-Low-Mem: true" \
  -d '{"input":"test","truncate":false}' https://api.redwood.inf/v1/embeddings
```

runtime log extract shows conversion latency median 18ms per request add-on (+ queuing), plus batch fragmentation causing avg_batch_size=4.

maria_oncall: mitigation options? three quick ones: 1) pin customers to explicit 1536 variant, 2) change routing policy to avoid conversion path, 3) ask customer to disable `prefer_low_mem` in SDK.

kai_infra: also we can add a short-term autoscaler tweak to increase 1536-capable pool in region. will take ~10m to scale.

anna_support: advised customer to disable `prefer_low_mem` and will watch for change; offered pinned variant if they prefer us to change routing.

josh_research: created minimal repro script and perf harness to quantify overhead. gist: https://internal-gists/repohash (redacted) — shows vectors/sec recover when routed fully to 1536 pool.

maria_oncall: action items:
- kai_infra to bump 1536 pool by +20% in region (ETA 10m)
- anna_support to confirm customer SDK toggle and test
- josh_research to run perf harness post-change and share numbers
- keep oncall looped for regressions

kai_infra: scaling started (scale-request id scale-379-1). watching queue_depth.

deploy-bot: scale-request scale-379-1: started this will add 6 pods.

anna_support: customer disabled `prefer_low_mem` flag and ran a quick smoke — they see vectors/sec jump to ~980k/s, batch size back to 10.

josh_research: perf harness confirms: before conversion path vectors/sec 420k/s, after routing ->1536 pool 970k/s, p99 latency improved. attaching numbers in follow-up.

maria_oncall: great — can we add a safety-check in router to prefer same-dim variants or reject request with clear 4xx if incompatible? conversion should be opt-in.

kai_infra: logged infra ticket INF-2026-115: `router: hard-fail on dim mismatch unless allow_dim_conversion=true` and will add telemetry for conversion_count.

anna_support: customer happy, will close after one more hour of monitoring. thanks all :thumbsup:

josh_research: note for postmortem: document SDK `prefer_low_mem` interaction and add a note in model onboarding checklist about variant compatibility and routing policy.

maria_oncall: marking incident RESOLVED after monitoring window if stable.

anna_support: closing thread in 60m if no regressions.
